chapter: Williams on hard times and money
title: Eating pepper grass in hard times
summary: Williams recalls chewing tough pepper grass for its juice when food was scarce.

story.theme_name: Making a living: hard times, day jobs and scarce work
story.community_name: The Depression years and the WPA band

blocks.x: What can 15 cents do? 15 cents can't get a cut of the back, but now. Sure. But I tell you what, I wished a lot of time, now I can see way back days, when things were really cheap. If I'd tell you all what I have did, you wouldn't believe me. Only time was hard. You ever heard of Tucker, Pepper Grace?

Sure. I have eaten, but it have grown out of season. It have run like a watermelon. And around, we have picked it and boiled it. It wouldn't get done. And eat that, drink the water off it, bite the bread. But we chew that, that, uh, Pepper Grace just like we chewing a cow chew a cud. You saw a cow chew a cud. Well, that's what we have chewed. Chew a cow. Oh, yes, yes. It was too, uh, tough to chew up the swallow. So we just chew and chew until we get the juice out and then we spit that out and throw it away and bite the bread and drink some juice.
But we still was eating. Time was really tough.
